summary: Rerunning the unmeasured design is the right call, but the stated cause of the build failure is wrong. Stage 1 explicitly passed -std=c++17 in extra_cuda_cflags; the -gencode flag the harvest saw came from torch's arch-flag diagnostic line. Torch then omits its own C++20 default, and the torch headers reject C++17. The builder must REPLACE (or drop) -std=c++17, not add -std=c++20 next to it.
justification: Evidence: on the stage-1 commit 8ba8624, _bulk build calls load_inline(..., extra_cuda_cflags=['-O3', '-lineinfo', '-std=c++17']), and the attempt file records the same flags. Log line 5, '[bulk] arch flags passed to nvcc: [-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a]', is the code's own print of torch's arch flags, not the full nvcc command. The host main.o got -std=c++20 because torch adds its default -std only when the caller gives none. For the .cu the caller gave c++17, and this image's torch requires C++20, hence the #error. So the 03:41Z harvest note and LESSONS 165 ('nvcc flags were only -gencode') misdiagnose the cause, even though the remedy 'pass -std=c++20' is close. Appending -std=c++20 while leaving -std=c++17 risks nvcc rejecting a redefined -std or keeping the wrong one. Delete the c++17 entry and either pass only -std=c++20 or pass no -std and let torch choose; the main.o line proves torch's choice is c++20. Base: 8ba8624^ has submission blob a8bb42a, identical to master's (8b9ad43), so the stage runs on current master as claimed. Design weakest link (unchanged from stage 1): every earlier stream stopped near 3.5 TB/s. pooler m<=16 at 19.0 us is already 67.1 MB / 19 us = 3.5 TB/s, and the 14.0 us floor implies ~4.8 TB/s, so M3 (16.5 us = 4.1 TB/s) needs ~85% of peak from a row-owner bulk stream. M1 (builds, PATH CHOSEN = bulk) and M2 are readable from one check; M3 is a stretch.
confounders: bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton (master): the m=32 pooler/unpooler incumbent is _bf16_swapab_kernel. Read those rows against this batch's swapab rows, since batch drift moved untouched small-m rows +2-6% together at 03:41Z.

router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m / bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo (master): they own the m<=16 pooler path (_bf16_splitk_kernel / _pooler_skinny) the bulk kernel replaces. Untouched layers (qkv_gate, o, router) are the in-run drift control.
bf16-restack-m16-swapab-router-swapab-m32 (BEST.json, unlanded): not this run's base. Identify the base from the kernel names in the profile (LESSONS 166), never from attribution base_result.
interference: No companion. The untouched layers in the same check are the drift control, and the replaced kernels are judged on their own profile rows. A second build-only run would duplicate the prepare print.
rules_flags: No rules concerns: same in-process load_inline, a lossless weight repack in prepare, and self-check against master with fallback unchanged.
open_questions: BUILDER: remove '-std=c++17' from extra_cuda_cflags and use ['-O3', '-lineinfo', '-std=c++20'] (or omit -std entirely). Do not append c++20 beside c++17. Keep TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a, and do not add a second -gencode since torch already emits it. Print the full nvcc command or flags list, and the last ~60 lines of the build log on failure (the current except keeps only str(e)[-600:]).
After it builds, assert in a one-call profiler probe that the launched kernel name is the bulk kernel for each gated (layer, m) (LESSONS 164), not just the PATH CHOSEN line.
Correct LESSONS 165 and the 03:41Z harvest note after the run: the cause was an explicit -std=c++17 override, not a missing flag.
